title: How a 1× gravel drivetrain spans mixed terrain
summary: Follow the single-chainring power path and see how a wide cassette provides both faster and lower climbing ratios.

steps.title: There is only one front chainring.
steps.body: Gravel G1 uses one front chainring, so front shifting disappears. All selectable ratios come from moving the chain across the rear cassette.
steps.keyFact: 1× simplifies the front drivetrain but places more of the total ratio range at the cassette.

steps.title: The cassette spans a wide range of sprocket sizes.
steps.body: Smaller rear sprockets create a higher gear for faster travel, while larger rear sprockets create a lower gear for climbing. Exact tooth counts and total range depend on the actual cassette and derailleur system.
steps.keyFact: Wide-range describes the spread of available rear ratios; it does not specify one universal tooth combination.

steps.title: The rear derailleur shifts and manages chain length.
steps.body: As the chain moves between cassette sprockets of different sizes, the derailleur guides lateral movement and takes up the resulting chain-length difference.
steps.keyFact: Derailleur compatibility depends on shifter actuation, cassette range, chain capacity, hanger interface and drivetrain generation.

steps.title: Wide range supports changing surfaces and gradients.
steps.body: A mixed-surface ride can move from fast pavement to steep loose climbs. A wide-range 1× system trades small ratio steps and front-shifting flexibility for a simpler control scheme and broad rear range.
steps.keyFact: No drivetrain architecture is universally best; gear range, step size, efficiency and simplicity are tradeoffs.

challenge.prompt: Where does Gravel G1 create its selectable gear ratios?

options.label: By shifting between multiple front chainrings
By shifting across the rear cassette

challenge.explanation: Gravel G1 is a 1× derailleur drivetrain: one front chainring and multiple rear cassette sprockets.

steps.title: Find the component that physically moves the chain across the cassette.
steps.body: Select the mechanism near the rear wheel that guides the chain between sprockets.
steps.keyFact: The handlebar control commands a shift; the rear derailleur performs the chain movement.

challenge.prompt: Which component moves the chain across the cassette?
challenge.successText: Correct. The rear derailleur guides the chain between cassette sprockets.
challenge.retryText: That part is involved in the drivetrain, but it does not guide the chain laterally between sprockets.
